title: Who Said What, and Will It Be Remembered? Evaluating Persistent Speaker Attribution Across Meetings
abstract: arXiv:2609.39344v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Speech transcripts used as long-term memory must preserve both words and stable speaker identities. Existing meeting-transcription metrics either ignore speakers or remap anonymous speakers independently in each recording, so they cannot measure whether the same person retains one identity across meetings. We evaluate persistent speaker attribution with Speaker Identified cpWER (SI-cpWER), which scores a corpus under one global speaker-ID assignment. The benchmark covers five commercial diarize-then-identify cascades, two open academic baselines, and ThyVoice on the full 129-meeting CHiME-8 NOTSOFAR evaluation set in clean and noiseaugmented form, plus CHiME-6. ThyVoice is our end-to-end reference system; it repairs overlap and gates the evidence used to create and update voiceprints. translated_title: 谁说了什么，这些会被记住吗？评估跨会议的持久说话人归属
translated_abstract: 用作长期记忆的语音转录必须同时保留词语内容和稳定的说话人身份。现有的会议转录指标要么忽略说话人，要么在每条录音中独立地重新映射匿名说话人，因此无法衡量同一个人在跨会议时是否保持同一身份。我们使用说话人识别cpWER（SI-cpWER）来评估持久说话人归属，该指标在单一的全局说话人ID分配下对整个语料库进行评分。该基准测试涵盖五种商业的先分离后识别级联系统、两个开放的学术基线系统，以及ThyVoice，评估集为完整的129场会议的CHiME-8 NOTSOFAR评估集（包括干净和噪声增强两种形式），以及CHiME-6。ThyVoice是我们的端到端参考系统；它修复重叠语音并对用于创建和更新声纹的证据进行门控。对持久身份的要求改变了商业系统的排名：在所有三种条件下，ThyVoice的SI-cpWER均低于所有被评估的商业级联系统。
tldr: 该论文提出SI-cpWER指标来评估同一说话人在跨会议场景下能否保持一致身份，并推出端到端参考系统ThyVoice，其在CHiME-8 NOTSOFAR全部三种测试条件下均取得优于所有被评估商业系统的表现。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes SI-cpWER to evaluate persistent speaker attribution across meetings and introduces ThyVoice, an end-to-end system that achieves lower SI-cpWER than all evaluated commercial cascades under all three conditions on the CHiME-8 NOTSOFAR benchmark.
